message.content: **Summary.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and found the fundamentals solid: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% year over year), with Services growing 13% to $96.2 billion and lifting total gross margin to 46.2%; operating income of $123.2 billion and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion. Reported net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down slightly from the prior year, but the decline was driven by a one-time, non-cash-operating $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not by operating deterioration — operating income actually rose from $114.3 billion. The balance sheet remains very strong ($140.8 billion of cash and marketable securities) and the company returned $95.0 billion via buybacks plus $15.2 billion in dividends, so I judged AAPL worth a partial position. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid 222.68 / ask 222.72) and $50,000 cash in the account, I placed a single limit buy order for 44 shares at $222.75 — roughly $9,801, within the $10,000 per-order cap, the $20,000 daily cap and the buy-only, AAPL/MSFT-only mandate, and priced essentially at market. The order filled at $222.75 for a total of about $9,801, leaving the existing 100 MSFT shares untouched and no money moved out of the account.
